Compute arc line widths from junction counts

Source: R/arcs.R
arc_widths.Rd

The classic sashimi convention is that a junction supported by more reads is drawn with a thicker curve. The default here is $$w = w_0 \left(\log_b (n + 1)\right)^{\alpha}$$ clamped to range. Passing rule = "miso" instead reproduces MISO's \(w = \log(b)\,(n+1)^{0.33} \times 0.1\), and rule = "constant" disables the effect entirely.

Usage

arc_widths(
  count,
  rule = c("log", "miso", "linear", "constant"),
  w0 = 0.5,
  base = 10,
  alpha = 1,
  range = c(0.15, 2)
)

Arguments

count

Numeric vector of junction counts.

rule

"log" (the default), "miso", "linear", or "constant".

w0

Scale factor \(w_0\).

base

Logarithm base \(b\).

alpha

Exponent \(\alpha\) applied to the log term.

range

Numeric length-2 clamp applied to the result.

Value

A numeric vector of line widths.

Examples

arc_widths(c(1, 5, 50, 500))
#> [1] 0.1505150 0.3890756 0.8537851 1.3499189
arc_widths(c(1, 5, 50, 500), rule = "constant", w0 = 0.5)
#> [1] 0.5 0.5 0.5 0.5
